title: React Performance Optimization: Memoization, Virtualization & Code Splitting
description: Eliminate unnecessary React re-renders with React.memo, useMemo, useCallback; virtualize large lists with TanStack Virtual; and reduce initial bundle size with Suspense-powered code splitting.

data.text: The cardinal rule of React performance engineering mirrors the .NET profiling rule: measure before you optimize. React DevTools Profiler records every render in your component tree, capturing render duration, component name, and the specific state or prop that triggered it. Adding React.memo, useMemo, and useCallback to components that are fast and rarely render actually adds overhead. Target components that re-render frequently with expensive computation or that render large datasets.

data.caption: Performance Optimization Decision Tree for React Components
data.code:
flowchart TD
    A[Component re-renders] --> B{Does DevTools Profiler show > 16ms render?}
    B -->|No| C[Leave as-is. Optimization is premature.]
    B -->|Yes| D{What is expensive?}
    D -->|Heavy computation from props| E[Wrap with React.memo + useMemo calculation]
    D -->|Callback refs causing child re-renders| F[Wrap callback with useCallback]
    D -->|Rendering thousands of list items| G[Implement List Virtualization with TanStack Virtual]
    D -->|Large component import on first load| H[Lazy load with React.lazy + Suspense]

data.text: `React.memo` performs a shallow equality check on props. When parent components pass object or array literals as props (e.g., `style={{ color: 'red' }}`), a new reference is created every render, defeating memo entirely. Always stabilize object references with `useMemo` and callback references with `useCallback`.

data.title: Correct Usage of React.memo with useMemo & useCallback
data.content: The CitationList component should only re-render when the actual citation data changes, not when the parent AI chat component streams a new token.

data.text: List Virtualization for AI Conversation History

Enterprise AI assistants accumulate hundreds of messages per conversation. Rendering 500 DOM nodes simultaneously causes layout thrash and scrolling stutters. List virtualization renders only the visible window (e.g., 10–15 items) while simulating the full scrollable height.

data.title: Virtualizing Chat History with TanStack Virtual
data.content: TanStack Virtual dynamically computes row heights to handle messages with variable content lengths including code blocks and markdown.

data.text: Heavy AI features like Markdown renderers, Mermaid diagram visualizers, or vector search result maps can easily add 200–500KB to the initial bundle. Loading them lazily on demand keeps the critical path bundle under 100KB.

data.title: Lazy Loading the Mermaid Diagram Renderer
data.content: Mermaid weighs ~180KB gzipped. Only load it when a diagram block is first encountered in the AI response stream.

data.caption: React Performance Optimization Techniques: When to Apply Each
rows: Expensive derived calculation run every render
Callback reference change defeats child memo
Large initial JS bundle on first page load

data.title: React Performance Optimization Audit
items: Profile component tree with React DevTools Profiler before adding any memoization
Stabilize object and array props with useMemo so React.memo's shallow equality check is effective
Stabilize callback props with useCallback only when the receiving child is wrapped with React.memo
Virtualize lists exceeding 50 dynamic-height items using TanStack Virtual
Split heavy editor, diagram, or analytics imports with React.lazy and Suspense fallbacks
Verify bundle composition with Vite visualizer or webpack-bundle-analyzer

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: Profile with React DevTools Profiler before applying any memoization.
React.memo requires stable prop references (useMemo/useCallback) to be effective.
TanStack Virtual eliminates DOM bloat from large message histories or search result lists.
Code splitting with React.lazy + Suspense keeps initial JS bundles lean and first-load fast.
data.takeaway: Performance optimization in React is empirical: measure with DevTools, identify the real hot path, and apply the minimal technique that resolves the specific bottleneck.
